title: Virtualization, Virtual Machines, and Containers
summary: Compare common infrastructure-abstraction concepts without administering production systems.
objectives: Explain the physical-server to virtual-machine relationship.
Compare containers and VMs at a conceptual level.

vocab.def: A virtualization layer that manages virtual machines on physical resources.
A computer-like environment that shares physical infrastructure through virtualization.
A package of an application and dependencies that shares more of the underlying operating system.

sections.heading: Share and isolate
sections.body: A physical server may host a virtualization layer and several VMs. This can consolidate workloads, allocate resources, and provide isolation concepts. It does not remove the need for capacity and operations.

sections.heading: Containers and VMs
sections.body: Containers often have less overhead by sharing more of the operating system, while VMs provide a different isolation boundary. Neither is universally better; the workload and policy matter.

practice.prompt: Why might an organization use a VM?
practice.answer: To isolate and allocate a computer-like workload while sharing physical infrastructure.

quiz.question: What does a container generally share more of than a VM?

lab.objective: Compare simulated VM and container placement choices.

futureCompetencyCandidates: compare virtualization abstractions for an infrastructure scenario
reflectionPrompt: What resource constraint still matters after a workload is virtualized?
